gloss: to make a profit; to gain a benefit

definitions.gloss: to make a profit; to earn a return
definitions.explanation: To come out financially ahead from a business, sale, or investment.

definitions.gloss: to gain a benefit; to profit from something
definitions.explanation: To obtain an advantage that need not be monetary — a favorable position, useful information, or an improved situation. Often used when pointing out who stands to gain from an arrangement.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{大|おお}きな{利益|りえき}を{得|え}た。
examples.english: The company made a large profit.

examples.japanese: {土地|とち}を{売|う}って{利益|りえき}を{得|え}たそうだ。
examples.english: I hear they made a profit by selling the land.

examples.japanese: {値上|ねあ}げをせずに{利益|りえき}を{得|え}るには、コストを{見直|みなお}すしかない。
examples.english: The only way to make a profit without raising prices is to review costs.

examples.japanese: {誰|だれ}が{利益|りえき}を{得|え}るのだろうか。
examples.english: Who stands to benefit, I wonder?

examples.japanese: この{制度|せいど}から{利益|りえき}を{得|え}ているのは{一部|いちぶ}の{人|ひと}だけだ。
examples.english: Only a small number of people benefit from this system.

examples.japanese: {両国|りょうこく}が{利益|りえき}を{得|え}られる{形|かたち}で{交渉|こうしょう}をまとめたいと{考|かんが}えている。
examples.english: They hope to conclude the negotiations in a way that lets both countries benefit.

notes:
A set phrase pairing {利益|りえき} (profit, benefit) with {得|え}る (to obtain). {得|え}る is a written-style verb, so the phrase belongs to news reporting, business writing, and formal speech; in conversation people say {儲|もう}かる or {得|とく}をする instead.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ...から{利益|りえき}を{得|え}る: to profit from ...
- {大|おお}きな{利益|りえき}を{得|え}る: to make a large profit
- {不当|ふとう}な{利益|りえき}を{得|え}る: to obtain an improper gain

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {利益|りえき}を{上|あ}げる: to raise profits — focuses on the company's own performance
- {儲|もう}かる: to be profitable — casual and intransitive; the money-maker is the subject
- {得|とく}をする: to come out ahead — casual, everyday advantage rather than accounted profit
